entries.reason: the release lists its devices in the order of the device types from iOS 11 on and unsorted for a program linked against iOS 10; a program built now is linked against a later release, so the port orders them as that one does
entries.effect: the devices come back in the order of the device types given, and inside one type by position, back before front
entries.source: AVFoundation of the armv7s cache of iOS 10.3.4, read method by method, and the host's own AVFoundation run beside the port through Mac Catalyst

entries.reason: the release reads the type from the capture source of the device, and the hardware of iOS 6 has one kind of camera and one microphone
entries.effect: a device that has video only is the wide angle camera, one that has audio only is the built-in microphone, and any other, which iOS 6 has none of, answers an empty string as the release's base class does

entries.reason: the class's OWN metadata carries -init, at every release measured, even though the SDK header closes it with AV_INIT_UNAVAILABLE (AVCaptureDevice.h:2841 in 26.2, :2368 in 16.4) and an unavailable redeclaration forces no definition - so the class's own method list decides. Measured with tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua over the held caches: 10.0.1 arm64 gives the class the own instance methods -_initWithDeviceTypes:mediaType:position:, -dealloc, -description, -devices, -init, and a metaclass list of one, +discoverySessionWithDeviceTypes:mediaType:position:; 12.0 and 16.0 still carry -init and the metaclass still never carries +new
entries.effect: nil, and no exception. Measured on the host's own class: [[AVCaptureDeviceDiscoverySession alloc] init] answers nil and +new answers nil, while the session an application can use comes from +discoverySessionWithDeviceTypes:mediaType:position:. The port answers nil for the same reason
entries.source: the class's own method list in the arm64e cache of iOS 16.0 and the arm64 cache of 10.0.1, read with tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua, and the host's own AVFoundation under tests/backports/host/unavailable-init

entries.reason: Apple's class does NOT implement it, at any release measured: the metaclass list holds one entry at 10.0.1 and never names +new at 12.0 or at 16.0. So this row is the inherited +[NSObject new] every class answers, and defining it in the port would put a selector in the port's metadata where Apple's class has none and answer the caller exactly what NSObject's already answers. Measured on the host too: new is in NSObject's own metaclass list of 115 entries and not in this class's metaclass list of 16
entries.effect: what +[NSObject new] answers, which is this class's own -init and therefore nil: measured on the host, +new answers nil and raises nothing. Nothing in the port defines +new
